pr_title: Escape formula path in ruby source url
pr_body:
- [x] Have you followed the guidelines in our [Contributing](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) document?
- [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pulls) for the same change?
- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [ ] Have you written new tests for your changes? [Here's an example](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/HEAD/Library/Homebrew/test/PATH_spec.rb).
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew style` with your changes locally?
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew typecheck` with your changes locally?
- [ ] Have you successfully run `brew tests` with your changes locally?

-----

Fixes #15235.

This was causing problems when trying to parse the formula name from the path when loading the formual. This didn't happen previously because downloading formula ruby source files from Github is a recent addition with the API changes.

The problem seems to come from the `AbstractFileDownloadStrategy#parse_basename` method which turns the plus symbols into spaces.

```rb
[7] brew(main)> formula = "bonnie++".f
=> #<Formula bonnie++ (stable) /opt/homebrew/Library/Taps/homebrew/homebrew-core/Formula/bonnie++.rb>
[8] brew(main)> resource = formula.resource("ruby-source"); nil
=> nil
[9] brew(main)> resource.url
=> "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula/bonnie++.rb"
[10] brew(main)> strategy = AbstractFileDownloadStrategy.new(nil, nil, nil); nil
=> nil
[11] brew(main)> strategy.send(:parse_basename, resource.url)
=> "bonnie  .rb"
```

It looks like it is caused by the use of `URI.decode_www_form_component`.

```rb
brew(main):005:0> url = "/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula/bonnie++.rb"
=> "/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula/bonnie++.rb"
brew(main):006:0> URI.decode_www_form_component(url)
=> "/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula/bonnie  .rb"
```

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ac0663ae5d2d4c76bb62363592d77dbad49ac30c/Library/Homebrew/download_strategy.rb#L352

Maybe we just need to escape the original URL better.

```rb
brew(main):010:0> url
=> "/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula/bonnie++.rb"
brew(main):011:0> URI.decode_www_form_component CGI.escape(url)
=> "/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula/bonnie++.rb"
```

That works but we don't actually want to escape the whole URL so we instead just escape the path when first creating the `ruby-source` resource.

Then, we must make sure the following works as expected. This is based on [this block of code](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/62d42c72f51fe08b8fe4aa25a13c59e82c77037e/Library/Homebrew/formula_installer.rb#L1196-L1205) that was failing previously.

```rb
[1] brew(main)> formula = "bonnie++".f
=> #<Formula bonnie++ (stable) /opt/homebrew/Library/Taps/homebrew/homebrew-core/Formula/bonnie++.rb>
[2] brew(main)> resource = formula.resource("ruby-source"); nil
=> nil
[3] brew(main)> resource.fetch; nil
==> Downloading https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/9fa25e536710603c675fe187c564cbaac45fb7d5/Formula%2Fbonnie%2B%2B.rb
######################################################################## 100.0%
=> nil
[4] brew(main)> source_formula = Formulary.factory(
[4] brew(main)*   resource.cached_download,
[4] brew(main)*   formula.active_spec_sym,
[4] brew(main)*   alias_path: formula.alias_path,
[4] brew(main)*   flags: formula.class.build_flags,
[4] brew(main)*   from: :formula_installer
[4] brew(main)* )
=> #<Formula bonnie++ (stable) /Users/kevinrobell/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/1f2743c88d65eadc21f39e76e0e1d493b333e0f150e7caeb3a89cb8be2a4280a--bonnie++.rb>
```
pr_comments: I just have to say, it's pretty weird that we define this as a resource of the formula itself, but I think that's already covered by https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/issues/14746.

Sorry but this is definitely a download strategy bug and not a formulary bug (the rewrite I made would have the exact same issue too) nor is it anything specific to formula rb downloads. As per the various RFCs, the plus character only means spaces in the query string portion of the URL. The `URI.decode_www_form_component` should only apply to that part of the URL - the whole URL is not a "form component". RFC3986-compliant URL decoding methods (e.g. ERB::Util) should be used instead for the path part - `URI.decode_www_form_component` is not one of them.

The plus is in the path part of the URL here so should be treated literally - curl etc will do so.

The code in question also seems like it would be buggy when dealing with URL-encoded `?` characters.
We vendor `addressable` now so we could use that if it's any easier - it probably does a lot of encoding/decoding automatically.

To demonstrate, I can take your steps to reproduce and show the same issue on the main URL for the formula too:

```ruby
brew(main):001:0> formula = "bonnie++".f
=> #<Formula bonnie++ (stable) /usr/local/Homebrew/Library/Taps/homebrew/homebrew-core/Formula/bonnie++.rb>
brew(main):002:0> formula.stable.url
=> "https://www.coker.com.au/bonnie++/bonnie++-2.00a.tgz"
brew(main):003:0> strategy = AbstractFileDownloadStrategy.new(nil, nil, nil); nil
=> nil
brew(main):004:0> strategy.send(:parse_basename, formula.stable.url)
=> "bonnie  -2.00a.tgz"
```

> I just have to say, it's pretty weird that we define this as a resource of the formula itself, but I think that's already covered by #14746.

Agreed. I'd love to see that cleaned up sooner rather than later.

Similarly, if we see (m)any more "from source from the API" only bugs: I'd prefer we just removed support for this. I didn't think it made sense to add at the time and niche edge-case bugs like this are the reason why.

> Similarly, if we see (m)any more "from source from the API" only bugs: I'd prefer we just removed support for this.

This feels a bit of an overreaction since it's been 2 months without a bug report and the one found here is one that's not from-source specific as it also affects casks.

> This feels a bit of an overreaction since it's been 2 months without a bug report

Yes but also the promised cleanups have never manifested and having these sort of issues that are so far off the beaten path doesn't provide a good user experience for anyone.

> one found here is one that's not from-source specific as it also affects casks.

Do you have reproduction instructions for a cask failing similarly? If so: that's another issue we'll need to address after this PR.

> > This feels a bit of an overreaction since it's been 2 months without a bug report
> 
> Yes but also the promised cleanups have never manifested and having these sort of issues that are so far off the beaten path doesn't provide a good user experience for anyone.

Similarly: this can be flipped as "this has been broken for all formulae with + in their names since the day it was merged/tagged and it's taken 2 months for anyone to encounter this: this points to this not being a widely used feature/flow".
This doesn't currently affect casks since casks are loaded from content using `curl_output`, so the filename doesn't matter.
Also I don't think we have any cask with a `+` in its name at the moment.

> This doesn't currently affect casks since casks are loaded from content using `curl_output`, so the filename doesn't matter.

Sorry I meant cask artifact downloads rather than Ruby source downloads - I was following up to how this affects the source archive of the formula too. Though for casks, individual casks work around this issue themselves by manual percent encoding (we've had various `version.sub("+", "%2B")` over the years).

#15258 is an attempt at fixing the core issue here.

> Similarly: this can be flipped as "this has been broken for all formulae with + in their names since the day it was merged/tagged and it's taken 2 months for anyone to encounter this: this points to this not being a widely used feature/flow".

Of the formulae with `+` in their names, only one doesn't have a relocatable bottle so it's not a widespread problem at all. (We haven't enabled the API for older macOS yet so relocatable bottles are the primary concern at the moment.)

If we want to continue arguing "nobody uses this": let's start adding analytics rather than guessing. (Side note: have we addressed why analytics numbers are down 99% over previous months?)

@Bo98 I'll leave this open for now but I agree that this doesn't fix the root of the problem. The difficult thing though is that `AbstractFileDownloadStrategy#parse_basename` has been broken for so long that I'm not immediately sure if changing the behavior will affect something else. I'll take a look at your PR.

> The difficult thing though is that `AbstractFileDownloadStrategy#parse_basename` has been broken for so long that I'm not immediately sure if changing the behavior will affect something else

Yes, that's always a risk. Though the same applies to things like the `version.rb` parser, which we've touched on multiple occasions (and still don't have a regression test for).

I could probably look at running a before & after comparison on all formulae and casks (tomorrow probably because it's 3am).
Closing in favor of #15258.

> If we want to continue arguing "nobody uses this": let's start adding analytics rather than guessing.

I'm not arguing "nobody uses this": I'm arguing that a very small proportion of our users do and, most importantly, it's not a use-case we support.

That will result in, like this, bugs that only emerge many months after the code is changed making them harder to debug and less likely the person who introduced them will be around for a timely fix.

Finally, it's not "guessing". I've worked on this project for just under 14 years now. I have a pretty good sense of what flows people use and what flows they don't. I'd rather not add more analytics to resolve an issue that isn't primarily numerical.

> Side note: have we addressed why analytics numbers are down 99% over previous months?

Most likely any/all of: we gave people a Google Analytics only opt-out, we fixed some double-reporting, we reminded people of our Google Analytics, we told them we'd be switching over to InfluxDB around now.

> Though the same applies to things like the `version.rb` parser, which we've touched on multiple occasions (and still don't have a regression test for).

We do have a pretty decent number of regression tests for `version.rb` handling.

Here's other things that are likely/possibly broken when installing from source using the API:
- references to `tap` (e.g. `tap.issues_url` in `gcc`)
- `Formula.[]` references to other formulae (e.g. doing `Formula["foo"].deps` inside formula `bar`)

There's probably more. It really would be simpler to just error out and tell the user they need to set `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API` than to try to catch these all.

Something to remember: we had _multiple_ open issues regarding build from source when the API is enabled prior to implementing this, largely from desync between JSON "git head" and local git head - it wasn't implemented because I was bored one night. Now we're at a rate of none in multiple months.

> * references to `tap` (e.g. `tap.issues_url` in `gcc`)

I asked about this at the time as this was the only behavioural difference and the answer then was parity with casks was desirable and casks had an identical issue. This is trivial to fix though and will push that to the refactor PR (so I don't have to fix it twice - but I'll make it a separate commit for visibility).

> * `Formula.[]` references to other formulae (e.g. doing `Formula["foo"].deps` inside formula `bar`)

Cannot reproduce. `brew install -s ocaml-zenith` executes `cp Formula["ocaml"].opt_lib/"ocaml/Makefile.config", lib/"ocaml"` fine.

> We do have a pretty decent number of regression tests for version.rb handling.

Various homebrew-core formulae have had unexpected version number changes after a change to the parser on multiple occasions, so unless a test was added in the last couple years I don't think that's addressed yet.

> Most likely any/all of: we gave people a Google Analytics only opt-out, we fixed some double-reporting, we reminded people of our Google Analytics, we told them we'd be switching over to InfluxDB around now.

1 million -> 10,000 was a lot more than I expected, but if it's been checked then fair enough!

> Something to remember: we had _multiple_ open issues regarding build from source when the API is enabled prior to implementing this, largely from desync between JSON "git head" and local git head - it wasn't implemented because I was bored one night. Now we're at a rate of none in multiple months.

I remember. Similarly, my proposed and at least partially implemented solution at the time was: if you build from source in any circumstance: you do not use the API. Similarly, something to remember: I suggested that having 2 paths:
- build from source, don't use API, what we do in CI
- use bottles, use API, what users mostly do

would be better than adding a third:
- build from source, use API, most users don't do this, we don't do this in CI

> Now we're at a rate of none in multiple months.

As I said above: this can be read as:
- this flow so so stable that we've only had one issue in multiple months
or:
- this flow is so niche that it takes multiple months to get an issue filed for something that has been broken that whole time

I'm not shitting on your work here and I'm not saying it should the "build from source using API" flow should all be ripped out today but: if I'd have known what this was going to look like, I would have argued harder for not doing this at the time.

Given [how many `install from api` issues we still have](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22install+from+api%22) I still think we've overextended ourselves here by expanding the number of paths and flows we support for users and we're not able to provide a good enough experience. That's not on you though, @Bo98, that's as much on me and every other maintainer.

> Various homebrew-core formulae have had unexpected version number changes after a change to the parser on multiple occasions, so unless a test was added in the last couple years I don't think that's addressed yet.

That we have some, pretty decent regression tests here does not make this flawless. You could indeed make a(nother) regression test that e.g. checked that every homebrew-core formula had the same version before and after any change, that's true. If performant enough, that would be a good unit test to have. This would make sense as a `help wanted` issue to investigate, I think. 

> 1 million -> 10,000 was a lot more than I expected, but if it's been checked then fair enough!

It hasn't been checked. I know there was double counting going on for a while because I fixed it. The rest is my hypothesis based on reading chatter around the internet about this. I'm not sure it's worth digging in much to Google Analytics considering the platform and code are disappearing imminently. If we're getting similar issues with InfluxDB now/after: we should dig in here and investigate more, I agree.

> Similarly, something to remember: I suggested that having 2 paths:
> 
> * build from source, don't use API, what we do in CI
> * use bottles, use API, what users mostly do

The problem here is again the desync issue.

You are installing bottles from one source and building from source from another source if you do it that way. You will need to make sure the JSON and the git repo are directly in line for this to work without issues, which may mean frequent auto-updates (but we set it to 24 hours). `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API` is only really safe if set universally for _all_ installs and any `brew update`.

Having the source information in the JSON instead meant that this problem was entirely eliminated. It's also more secure as we sign the JSON but do not, despite our best intentions, sign git repos sufficiently.

The security and speed benefits is why I want to enable API for everyone before macOS 11 is dropped, but I will not pursue that before the summer.

In any case, this is all getting refactored anyway so let's see how that goes.

> `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API` is only really safe if set universally for _all_ installs and any `brew update`.

Yes, we agree here. I think setting it selectively for specific commands is non-ideal.

> Having the source information in the JSON instead meant that this problem was entirely eliminated. It's also more secure as we sign the JSON but do not, despite our best intentions, sign git repos sufficiently.

I gently disagree here but it's sufficiently off-topic that I don't think we should get into it here.

> The security and speed benefits is why I want to enable API for everyone before macOS 11 is dropped, but I will not pursue that before the summer.

To beat you to it: I'm extremely strongly opposed to this work being done until we have no open `install from api` issues, are able to merge https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/14592 accordingly and, even then, I may not be convinced it's a good idea.

Putting more time an effort into unsupported OSs, prefixes and other configurations is not a good use of our time.

> I'm extremely strongly opposed to this work being done until we have no open `install from api` issues

Yeah I should mentioned sorry, but I do agree with that: yes.

> Putting more time an effort into unsupported OSs, prefixes and other configurations is not a good use of our time.

Removing the conditional that treats them differently in a way helps with that.

> > I'm extremely strongly opposed to this work being done until we have no open `install from api` issues
> 
> Yeah I should mentioned sorry, but I do agree with that: yes.

No worries: glad we're aligned ❤️ 

> > Putting more time an effort into unsupported OSs, prefixes and other configurations is not a good use of our time.
> 
> Removing the conditional that treats them differently in a way helps with that.

Somewhat/perhaps? We're always going to need to have a "not using the API and installing from a Git repository" flow for at least homebrew-core/homebrew-cask CI and contribution, no?

comments:
Would it be possible for you to to try those commands again with the `--debug` flag? That might show some more helpful information.

I tried reinstalling the `bonnie++` package locally and that worked as expected so I'm wondering if this might possibly be API related somehow (just a wild guess).

Either way from the output it seems to be failing somewhere in the fetch stage for some reason. We know this because it never reached the `Reinstalling <formula_name>...` part of the messaging.

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ad3d207172639396b8585899c43be97d08f58709/Library/Homebrew/reinstall.rb#L60-L62

The fetch code inside the installer fetches the formula source (the JSON formula representation doesn't contain the info necessary to build from source) and then reloads the formula using it. It seems to fail to load the formula the second time.

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/ad3d207172639396b8585899c43be97d08f58709/Library/Homebrew/formula_installer.rb#L1200-L1204
